He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]], where he tied the freshman [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) three-point field goal record and achieved a new general Razorback best with 113 shots from distance made in a single season.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Isaiah-Joe-Arkansas-Razorbacks-playmaking-ability-Red-White-Game-136611366/|title=Isaiah Joe displays playmaking ability|first=Pete|last=Roulier|date=October 6, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Joe was selected in the second round of the [[2020 NBA Draft]] with the 49th overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. After two seasons with the 76ers, he was waived and joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], winning a championship with them in [[2025 NBA Finals|2025]]. ==Early life== Joe grew up in [[Fort Smith, Arkansas]], where he attended [[Northside High School (Fort Smith, Arkansas)|Northside High School]] alongside [[Jaylin Williams (basketball, born 2002)|Jaylin Williams]], his now professional teammate.{{cite web|url=https://www.vanburencountydem.com/sports/20190313/ua-basketball-everyday-joe-ignites-hogs?template=ampart|title=UA Basketball: 'Everyday Joe' ignites Hogs|work=Van Buren County Democrat|date=March 13, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{Dead link|date=February 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} He shot 41% from three-point range in his sophomore season and committed to play [[college basketball]] at the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|University of Arkansas]] during the summer going into his junior year over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Arkansas-Little Rock]].{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasfight.com/2016/8/2/12364674/arkansas-basketball-recruiting-isaiah-joe-commits-razorbacks|title=Arkansas Basketball Recruiting: Isaiah Joe Commits to the Razorbacks|first=Doc|last=Harper|website=ArkansasFight.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=August 2, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2019}} As a junior, Joe averaged 18.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.2 steals per game and helped lead the Grizzlies to an [[Arkansas Activities Association]] (AAA) 7A state championship and was named first-team All-State.{{cite web|url=https://5newsonline.com/2017/11/08/northsides-isaiah-joe-signs-with-razorbacks/|title=Northside's Isaiah Joe Signs With Razorbacks|first=Brooke|last=Grimsley|website=[[KFSM-TV|5NewsOnline.com]]|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=November 13, 2019}} As a senior, Joe averaged 22.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 2.9 steals per game and was named the Gatorade Arkansas Boys Basketball Player of the Year and the State Player of the Year by [[USA Today]] as he led Northside to the state title game before eventually falling to [[North Little Rock High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20180309/basketball-northsides-joe-named-gatorade-player-of-year|title=Basketball: Northside's Joe named Gatorade Player of the Year|first=Buck|last=Ringgold|work=[[Southwest Times Record]]|date=March 9, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019|archive-date=November 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191113164255/https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20180309/basketball-northsides-joe-named-gatorade-player-of-year|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-arkansas-boys-basketball-team|title=2017–18 ALL-USA Arkansas Boys Basketball Team|first=Evan|last=Hilbert|website=[[USA Today|USATodayHSS.com]]|date=April 16, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} ==College career== Joe averaged 13.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.5 steals per game over 34 games played as a freshman and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman team.{{cite web|url=https://www.kait8.com/2019/03/13/arkansas-guard-isaiah-joe-named-sec-all-freshman-team/|title=Arkansas guard Isaiah Joe named to SEC All-Freshman Team|website=[[KAIT|KAIT.com]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} He made 113 [[three-pointer]]s on 273 attempts (41.4%), breaking the Arkansas record previously held by [[Scotty Thurman]] (102) and tying the record for a freshman in the SEC while also leading the conference in three-point percentage.{{cite news|url=https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20191007/steady-joe-impresses-new-coach|title=Steady Joe impresses new coach|work=[[Southwest Times Record]]|date=October 7, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019|archive-date=November 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191113162208/https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20191007/steady-joe-impresses-new-coach|url-status=dead}}{{cite web |title=Isaiah Joe, Philadelphia, Shooting Guard |url=https://247sports.com/player/isaiah-joe-45572684/ |website=247sports.com |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=1 July 2026}} He was also named the SEC Player of the Week after scoring 34 points on 10 of 13 shooting from three (11–14 overall) against [[2018–19 FIU Panthers men's basketball team|FIU]] on December 1, 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.4029tv.com/article/isaiah-joe-earns-sec-player-of-the-week-honor/25384179|title=Isaiah Joe earns SEC Player of the Week honor|first=Jourdan|last=Black|website=[[KHBS|4029TV.com]]|date=December 3, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Entering his sophomore season, Joe was named preseason All-SEC and to [[Jerry West Award]] watchlist.{{cite news|url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/nov/05/isaiah-joe-makes-coaches-preseason-all-/|title=Isaiah Joe makes coaches' preseason all-SEC team|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://razorbackers.com/2019/10/16/razorback-basketball-isaiah-joe-named-to-jerry-west-award-watch-list/|title=Razorback Basketball: Isaiah Joe named to Jerry West Award Watch List|first=Easton|last=Leonard|website=RazorBackers.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]}} Joe was also named the 80th-best collegiate basketball player going into the 2019–20 season by [[CBS Sports]] and the 33rd-best prospect for the [[2020 NBA draft]] by [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ranking-the-top-100-and-1-best-players-in-college-basketball-entering-the-2019-20-season/|title=Ranking the Top 100 And 1 best players in college basketball entering the 2019–20 season|first1=Kyle|last1=Boone|first2=Matt|last2=Norlander|first3=Gary|last3=Parrish|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 24, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/27998169/nba-mock-draft-viewer-guide-our-top-prospects|title=NBA mock draft: Viewer's guide for our top prospects|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 4, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Joe was named the SEC co-Player of the Week on January 2, 2020, following a 24-point, five rebound performance in a 71–64 win against [[2019–20 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thv11.com/article/sports/isaiah-joe-named-sec-co-player-of-the-week/91-f1135f0c-a18b-4972-b98d-86db46970215|title=Isaiah Joe named SEC Co-Player of the Week|website=[[KTHV|THV11.com]]|date=December 30, 2019|access-date=January 2, 2020}} Joe scored 34 points, including 26 in the second half, on January 12 to lead Arkansas in a 76–72 comeback win over [[2019–20 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Isaiah-Joe-Arkansas-Razorbacks-Ole-Miss-Rebels--142084524/|title=Isaiah Joe wills Razorbacks to victory over Rebels|first=Pete|last=Rouler|website=247Sports.com|date=January 12, 2020|access-date=January 17, 2020}} On February 4, Joe underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his knee after an MRI revealed inflammation and was ruled out indefinitely.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Arkansas star Isaiah Joe, a potential first-round NBA Draft pick, out indefinitely after knee surgery |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/arkansas-star-isaiah-joe-a-potential-first-round-nba-draft-pick-out-indefinitely-after-knee-surgery/ |access-date=February 5, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 4, 2020}} As a sophomore, Joe averaged 16.9 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Roulier |first1=Pete |title=Joe lands low on ESPN's draft board |url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Isaiah-Joe-NBA-Draft-ESPN-mock--145900259/ |access-date=April 14, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=April 10, 2020}} Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Arkansas' Isaiah Joe declares for 2020 NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/20/arkansas-isaiah-joe-declares-for-2020-nba-draft/ |access-date=April 21, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 20, 2020}} On August 1, Joe announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to Arkansas.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Isaiah Joe withdraws from NBA draft, returning to Arkansas |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29578413/isaiah-joe-withdraws-draft-returning-arkansas |access-date=August 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=August 1, 2020}} However, on August 17 he reversed course and left Arkansas for the professional ranks.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=2020 NBA Draft: Arkansas standout Isaiah Joe reverses course, re-enters draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2020-nba-draft-arkansas-standout-isaiah-joe-reverses-course-re-enters-draft/ |access-date=October 23, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=August 17, 2020}} Joe is also a member of the [[Phi Beta Sigma]] fraternity. ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2022)=== [[File:Isaiah Joe (51827251346) (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|231x231px|Joe with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2022]] Joe was selected with the 49th overall pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |title=Team Selects Tyrese Maxey, Isaiah Joe, and Paul Reed |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-selects-tyrese-maxey-isaiah-joe-and-paul-reed |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 4, 2020 |date=November 18, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2171192/2020/11/18/isaiah-joe-philadelphia-76ers-nba-draft-rookie/|title=Isaiah Joe goes to the Philadelphia 76ers: Here's what they're getting|first=Brian|last=Bennett|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020}} On December 3, he signed with the 76ers.{{cite web |title=Team Signs Maxey, Joe, Reed |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-maxey-joe-reed |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 4, 2020 |date=December 3, 2020}} Joe made his NBA debut on December 27, 2020, playing seven minutes and scoring two points on 1-of-2 shooting with one rebound, one assist, and one steal in a 118–94 loss to the [[2020–21 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202012270CLE.html|title=Philadelphia 76ers at Cleveland Cavaliers Box Score, December 27, 2020|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 10, 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/trip-ends-loss-cavaliers|title=Trip Ends With Loss to Cavaliers|first=Lauren|last=Rosen|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2020|access-date=January 10, 2021}} He made 41 appearances (including one start) for Philadelphia during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 3.7 points, 0.9 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Joe 2020-21 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4395702/type/nba/year/2021|access-date=June 13, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Joe played in 55 games (including one start) for the 76ers in the [[2021–22 NBA season]], averaging 3.6 points, 1.0 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Joe 2021-22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4395702/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=June 13, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On October 13, 2022, he was waived by Philadelphia.{{cite web |last=Grasso |first=Justin |title=Sixers Move On From Young Sharpshooter Isaiah Joe |url=https://www.si.com/nba/76ers/news/sixers-waive-young-sharpshooter-isaiah-joe |website=Sports Illustrated |date=October 13, 2022 |access-date=October 13, 2022}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2022–2026)=== On October 16, 2022, Joe signed a deal with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Isaiah Joe|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-joe-221016|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2022|access-date=October 16, 2022}} On February 24, 2023, Joe scored a then career-high 28 points in a 124–115 loss to the [[2022–23 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Mussatto|title=Isaiah Joe scores career-high 28 points, but Thunder falls short at Suns|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/nba/thunder/2023/02/24/thunder-vs-suns-score-nba-game-recap-shai-gilgeous-alexander-injury/69942007007/|work=The Oklahoman|date=February 24, 2023|access-date=February 24, 2023}} On March 29, 2023, Joe put up a career-high 33 points in a 137–134 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-isaiah-joe-pops-for-career-high-33-points/#|title=Thunder's Isaiah Joe: Pops for career-high 33 points|website=CBS Sports|date=March 29, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2025}} On November 16, Joe made all seven of his three-point attempts en route to 23 points in a 128–109 win against the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite news|first=Sonja|last=Chen|title=Isaiah Joe goes 7 for 7 on 3-pointers, Thunder send short-handed Warriors to fifth straight loss|url=https://apnews.com/article/thunder-warriors-f1da38ce0b86feb10acdef5998562adc|work=Associated Press|date=November 17, 2023|accessdate=November 18, 2023}} On July 1, 2024, Joe re-signed with the Thunder on a four-year, $48 million contract.{{cite web | last=Almanza | first=Clemente | title=Report: OKC Thunder signs Isaiah Joe to four-year, $48 million deal | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2024-07-01 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/report-okc-thunder-signs-isaiah-135019538.html | access-date=2025-12-07}} On January 10, 2025, Joe scored 31 points on 11-of-16 shooting, connecting on a career-high eight three-pointers made in a 126–101 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-news-mark-daigneaults-honest-take-isaiah-joe-career-best-shooting|title=Thunder coach Mark Daigneault's honest take on Isaiah Joe's career-best shooting|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pavon|first=Josue|date=January 11, 2025|access-date=January 11, 2025}} On June 22, 2025, Joe won his first NBA championship defeating the Indiana Pacers 103–91 in Game 7 of the NBA Finals. Although he did not appear in Game 7, Joe was part of the Thunder’s roster and contributed throughout the playoffs, averaging 6.4 points per game and shooting 41.1 percent from three-point range over 21 appearances.{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/isaiah-joe-s-dad-recalls-son-s-rise-from-underdog-to-nba-champion/vi-AA1HhqsB?ocid=BingNewsSerp |access-date=2025-06-27
